project_ideas.name: State-vs-Transcript Diagnosis Study

project_ideas.name: Coordination-Overhead Tracer for Spatial Multi-Agent Systems
project_ideas.poc: Extend a persona-based multi-agent canvas setup (configurable agent attributes plus one orchestrator) with tracing of every assignment, claim, and action, then sweep agent count on a fixed task set and attribute wasted actions to coordination rather than task difficulty.

summary.html:
Overview

  • Speaker: Max Drake
  • Channel: AI Engineer
  • Main topic: Agents on the Canvas and Spatial User Interfaces for AI
  • Purpose: To demonstrate how tldraw's infinite canvas and SDKs serve as a spatial harness for AI agents, enabling multi-agent collaboration, spatial task management, and multimodal UI interactions. Max Drake, product engineer at tldraw, explores the intersection of AI agents and infinite canvas applications. He discusses why agents struggle in 2D space, the development of tldraw's infinite canvas SDKs as an agent engine, teaching LLMs about canvas geometry and interaction via 'teach' and agent starter kits, and multi-agent human collaboration through experimental 'fairies' systems.

Topic Map

Introduction to Agents on the Canvas

  • Explanation: Opening demo where Max Drake asks Claude Code to find a Notion document from an email and build it on the tldraw desktop app.
  • Key claims:
    • Agents can be directed to find documents and build applications on spatial canvases.
    • Canvas interfaces offer unique UX benefits when working with LLMs.
  • Examples:
    • Finding a Notion link from an email and building a fluid simulation demo.
  • Terminology:
    • tldraw desktop app
    • Notion document
    • Claude Code
  • Why it matters: Demonstrates the practical workflow of instructing coding agents to build UI prototypes directly within a spatial canvas app.

Background on tldraw and Infinite Canvas SDKs

  • Explanation: Overview of tldraw as a startup based in London, providing free infinite canvas whiteboarding apps and developer SDKs.
  • Key claims:
    • Getting infinite canvas mathematics and scaling right is difficult.
    • tldraw SDK acts as the engine powering many collaborative apps and AI canvas integrations.
  • Examples:
    • Miro competitors, slide designers, and Replit's agent canvas built on top of tldraw.
  • Terminology:
    • infinite canvas SDK
    • multiplayer built-in
    • live sync
  • Why it matters: Establishes why tldraw is uniquely positioned to solve the canvas-rendering bottleneck for AI applications.

Why Agents Struggle in 2D Space

  • Explanation: Analysis of why text-in/text-out coding agents fail at UI and alignment tasks in 2D canvas environments without specialized tooling.
  • Key claims:
    • Agents are trained on text-in/text-out and struggle to understand 2D spatial relationships.
    • Aligning UI elements requires significant engineering work to bridge agents with visual space.
  • Examples:
    • Trying to get LLM agents to align shapes or design visual components.
  • Terminology:
    • 2D space
    • UI alignment
    • matrix math
  • Why it matters: Highlights the fundamental mismatch between text-trained LLMs and spatial visual interfaces.

Teaching LLMs About the Canvas (Teach & Agent Starter Kit)

  • Explanation: Explanation of projects like 'teach' and the tldraw agent starter kit designed to teach LLMs about canvas DOM structures and screenshots.
  • Key claims:
    • Teaching LLMs about canvas structure involves combining screenshots, JSON data, and spatial prompts.
    • The agent starter kit wraps LLMs in a harness enabling them to work agentially on the canvas.
  • Examples:
    • Prompting a cat agent to bring red shapes over from elsewhere on the canvas.
  • Terminology:
    • agent starter kit
    • teach project
    • DOM structure
    • MIT license
  • Why it matters: Provides developers with open-source tools to turn standard LLMs into canvas-aware agents.

Multi-Agent Collaboration: Fairies

  • Explanation: Introduction of 'fairies', a multi-agent collaboration project where individual agent entities ('fairies') collaborate with humans and each other on the canvas.
  • Key claims:
    • Fairies can be configured, given attributes like hats or colors, and assigned tasks.
    • Multi-agent coordination allows users to inspect agent state without reading raw chat logs.
  • Examples:
    • Assigning financial memo tasks to a group of fairy agents.
  • Terminology:
    • fairies
    • orchestrator fairy
    • group chat
    • multi-agent coordination
  • Why it matters: Reimagines multi-agent interactions as visible, collaborative spatial entities rather than opaque chat windows.

The Spatial Harness and Dependency Graphs

  • Explanation: Discussion of internal hackathons at tldraw, dependency graphs for product launches, and the 'tech tree' app for task management.
  • Key claims:
    • Complex launches use massive dependency graphs to track tasks.
    • The tech tree app treats individual dependency graph tasks as autonomous coding agents.
  • Examples:
    • Hand tracking canvas controls and paddle ball games built via desktop app windows.
  • Terminology:
    • tech tree app
    • dependency graph
    • tldraw desktop app
    • code mode
  • Why it matters: Shows how spatial task trees can act as a fully functional project management and execution environment.

Key Points

Agents Are Bad at 2D Space

  • Explanation: Because LLMs are trained on text-in/text-out, they lack native intuition for 2D spatial positioning, resizing, and UI alignment.
  • Evidence: Developers encounter repeated failure modes when asking agents to build canvas apps without spatial harnesses.
  • Practical implication: Engineers must build custom spatial wrappers and tools so agents can perceive and manipulate canvas geometry.

The Canvas as a Spatial Harness

  • Explanation: Treating the infinite canvas as an agent runtime environment provides a shared workspace for humans and multiple AI agents.
  • Evidence: tldraw's SDK supports multiplayer live sync, cursors, and viewports out of the box.
  • Practical implication: Canvas apps become powerful interfaces for orchestrating multi-agent systems visually.

State Over Chat Logs

  • Explanation: In multi-agent spatial setups, users can inspect agent states directly on the canvas rather than digging through lengthy chat interfaces.
  • Evidence: Fairy agents show planning status, assigned tasks, and progress directly next to their visual avatars.
  • Practical implication: Improves observability and transparency in complex multi-agent workflows.

Frameworks, Models & Processes

tldraw Infinite Canvas SDK

  • How it works: Provides core primitives for selection, transformation, rendering, and multiplayer live synchronization in infinite 2D space.
  • Components:
    • Infinite canvas engine
    • Multiplayer live sync
    • Selection and viewpoint management
    • Agent runner harness
  • When to use: When building collaborative tools, design apps, whiteboards, or spatial agent interfaces.

Examples & Case Studies

Prompting an agent with a grey cat drawing to find red shapes elsewhere on the canvas.

  • Illustrates: Agent visual perception and goal-seeking behavior in spatial environments.
  • Lesson: Agents can navigate canvas viewports, identify target shapes, and execute spatial movement tasks.

Creating a multi-fairy group chat to draft financial memo figures for an upcoming board meeting.

  • Illustrates: Multi-agent task distribution and orchestration on the canvas.
  • Lesson: Specialized agents can coordinate subtasks, assign work, and report completion status visually.

Using tldraw desktop app as a tiling window manager to run code and play games like Pong.

  • Illustrates: Exposing desktop application instances and file systems to coding agents.
  • Lesson: Agents with computer access can manipulate OS-level windows and ephemeral UIs.

Actionable Takeaways

  • Immediate:
    • Explore the tldraw agent starter kit and MIT-licensed code on their website.
    • Experiment with combining screenshots and JSON canvas data for agent prompting.
  • Strategic:
    • Infinite canvases are emerging as primary user interfaces for multi-agent orchestration.
    • Bridging text-based LLMs with spatial primitives unlocks new paradigms in software design and project management.
  • Questions to investigate:
    • How do spatial harnesses scale when managing hundreds of concurrent agents?
    • What are the latency and token overhead costs of screenshot-based spatial reasoning?

Claims Worth Verifying

  • tldraw SDK powers agent canvas experiences for tools like Replit. (factual)
  • The agent starter kit code is available under an MIT license. (factual)

Notable Quotes

"am i qualified to be giving this talk? I like to think so. I've been doing like agents on the canvas stuff since before chatgpt came out." (at 1:45) "it turns out agents are really really bad at working in 2D space and understanding 2D space." (at 7:34) "fairies have friends, right? And they can here we go. And they can fairies can work together." (at 15:32)

Compressed Summary

  • Infinite canvases solve the spatial reasoning bottleneck for AI agents.
  • tldraw provides SDKs and agent starter kits for building canvas-native AI apps.
  • Multi-agent 'fairies' enable visual collaboration between humans and AI agents.
  • Spatial task trees and desktop app integrations allow agents to manage real-world workflows.
  • Keywords: tldraw, canvas, agents, spatial, multiplayer
  • Core insight: Treating the infinite canvas as a spatial harness bridges the gap between text-based LLMs and 2D visual software engineering.
